reviews.text: No matter how good a doctor is, treatment is a different matter.

I was taking care of my cat's treatment. Initially, after tests, they suspected a different illness, which I thought was strange, so I took her to another vet. Thanks to their patient and attentive care, which focused on my family and my cat, she recovered completely, and I was so happy. They answered all my questions accurately, which gave me a great sense of security.

They don't perform unnecessary tests and only provide the essential treatment, so I have a lot of trust in this vet.

At my previous hospital, they would give my child a thorough check of their joints and mouth (due to a history of surgery) during vaccinations, so I was a little surprised by the difference. The young male doctor gave me a somewhat cold impression.

The female doctor, however, spoke to me attentively about things other than vaccinations.

My beloved dog developed osteonecrosis of the femoral head and was operated on by Dr. Kishigami. I was honored that he put my dog's health first and performed the surgery that only he could. Thank you so much.

I was left with paralysis due to encephalitis, so I requested stem cells.
My kidney values ​​were also bad, but the paralysis improved and my kidney values ​​even returned to normal for a while, so I felt the treatment was effective.
I had five treatments over about three and a half months, and although it was expensive, I felt it was very effective and am very grateful.
When the director went on parental leave, I asked the deputy director to take over, and the handover was smooth. Both doctors were very kind, knowledgeable, and wonderful.
My son eventually passed away suddenly, but when I called to inform him of his death, the deputy director kindly took over the phone and carefully explained the possible causes.
The nurses were all very nice, so I think this is a very trustworthy hospital.

I honestly don't want to give it even one star, but I'm writing this review to prevent any more victims.
The service was terrible.
I went there almost every day for a month, but all they did was perform tests, take blood samples, and administer IVs; they only cared about making money.
I waited over two weeks for the test results, but the test results were wrong. (The re-tests were also shoddy.)
Upon arriving at the hospital, they ran out of chemotherapy drugs right before administering them. The veterinarians' responses varied greatly; some were terrible, providing only minimal explanations and showing no empathy for either the patient or the pet. Even worse, the nurses referred to the pets as "that thing."
However, they would use the honorific "chan" for pets they liked.
It truly felt like an assembly line; they showed no empathy whatsoever. They didn't check on the effectiveness of the chemotherapy or the pet's condition, and instead of once a week, the next chemotherapy was scheduled for three days later. I strongly recommend going to a different hospital if you're considering this one.
Every veterinarian makes suggestions that truly consider the well-being of the dogs, cats, and their owners.

I was very troubled when Sakai Veterinary Hospital closed, but after searching everywhere, I found a veterinary hospital that is suitable for my dog.

It's far from my house, but I decided on this one.

My dog ​​has patellar luxation and otitis externa. This veterinary hospital specializes in orthopedics, cancer treatment, rehabilitation, etc. The fees aren't unnecessarily high, and they're open on weekends and holidays. You can make reservations online.

I've never been there for a checkup, so I don't know for sure, but even though there's a coin-operated parking lot next door, cars waiting for appointments are always parked in a row.

I think to myself, "They can pay for the hospital, but they won't pay for parking, and the hospital doesn't do anything about it. They're both the kind of people who are at that level."

Additional information:
They report bicycles parked outside the hospital to the police, but they don't say anything about cars parked on the street by patients making house calls? That's the kind of hospital it is.

My 13-year-old dog, who lived at my parents' house, dislocated its joint and was walking on three legs. We were told it needed expensive surgery, so we went to Kishigami Hospital for a second opinion. They decided to try treatment without surgery first, and after about six months, the dog was able to walk on all four legs again. I am very grateful that they chose treatment over surgery, especially considering the dog's age. Thank you very much.

I moved nearby and this was my first visit, so I'd like to have my cat vaccinated once a year. I made an appointment by phone a few days before. I also told them that this wasn't the first time the cat had been vaccinated.

Because the doctor is young, I'm writing this without any bias. The cat was shaking, but the planning was poor. Even though I let him out of the carrier first, he didn't even bother to examine him.
He offered him some treats, which made me feel like I was a considerate doctor, but he refused to eat them because he was shaking. Just when I thought he'd finally started to examine him, he said he'd call a nurse to the back to give him more treats! Why didn't he realize that he was nervous and not eating?
He wasn't hissing or anything, he was just shaking, so couldn't he have just called out to him quickly?
I was the one who called out to him too.
I began to worry whether he was properly examined. Then he went back to get the vaccine again and didn't come back. Why didn't he have it ready?
And he gave me the vaccine without even taking my temperature.
I've been to many hospitals for my pet cats and rescue cats, but this was the first time they didn't even take their temperature.
And yet the initial consultation fee was 2,000 yen, and the fee for creating a medical record was 660 yen. I'm writing this down so that it's helpful for people who are planning to go there in the future.

Finally, this has nothing to do with the vet, but the cashier also gave me the wrong (higher) price, and when I handed it over as is, they said, "Huh? Even if you gave me this, we'll just give you back the XXX yen." I was like, "Huh?" So I asked, "You said XXX yen, right?" and they gave me a completely different price than the one on the calculator.
The cashier didn't apologize, they just said, "Oh, I see," and showed me the calculator with the correct price. Some people might think I misheard, but I clearly confirmed it by the mysterious price difference of XXX thousand XXX yen!
No, at least they should have apologized...

I'm never going there again. I'll go to the hospital before I moved, even if I have to pay for a taxi.
It seems like there are many people who trust the hospital and go there, so I was hesitant to write anything negative about it, but I realized that there are hospitals that can make people feel this anxious just about vaccines.

We've had several dogs treated here, and the staff, nurses, and doctors were all incredibly kind and attentive! If we didn't understand something, they would explain it to us in a clear and polite manner until we did. We were also very happy that they displayed a plaque commemorating our dog's longevity. When we called to express our gratitude at the end, they even sent us flowers, and we are so glad we chose this hospital. We truly believe it is an excellent animal hospital.
This is a kind, clean, and reassuring animal hospital!

On the way to the hospital, he was walking briskly as usual, admiring the scenery in a good mood, but that day he had indigestion. He had said from the first visit that he was timid, but it seems they forced him to take Barium because he was quiet, and he started acting strangely. We immediately took him to the emergency room, and when they asked if he had a heart problem, he replied that he just had a small murmur. That was also Kishigami. They tried hard to revive his heart, but he passed away. At the funeral, they said that the Barium had made his belly the size of a pregnant woman in her final month.

Dr. Suzuki is incredibly dedicated and considers the animals' feelings when treating them. He also explains things clearly and thoroughly to the families, and is a very caring and considerate doctor, so we feel at ease.

The waiting time is way too long. The consultation takes 30 minutes, but I have to wait over an hour for my medication. It's quite painful. The doctor is skilled and caring, and he's been treating me for a long time, so that's very helpful.
